name: Madagascar
sources: PROVENANCE NOTE FOR EVERY WORLD BANK FIGURE IN THIS FILE AND IN THE OTHER FOUR ON THIS BRANCH. api.worldbank.org and data.worldbank.org were both returning a WAF block page to this session for the whole of it - every request, every indicator, curl and fetch alike. The World Bank series named below were therefore read off IndexMundi's country tables, which republish WDI by indicator code (www.indexmundi.com/facts/<country>/indicator/<CODE>). The indicator codes and the values are the World Bank's; the vintage is IndexMundi's snapshot rather than today's WDI, and that is the risk this note exists to declare. Where a figure looked unlike the country, it was checked against neighbouring years from the same table rather than accepted on its own - see the investment note below, which is the one place on this branch where that check found something.

GDP $3.93bn: World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.CD, series MDG, 1990 = 3,931,335,000. On 11.6m people that is about $339 a head - THE POOREST NATION ON THIS BRANCH BY A FACTOR OF SEVEN and among the poorest in the roster. Madagascar is the one large state here: it holds 89% of the five nations' combined population and 74% of their combined output, and the other four together are smaller than a mid-sized African city.
Population 11.6m: World Bank SP.POP.TOTL, series MDG, 1990 = 11,598,650.

TFP trend -0.005: NEGATIVE, deliberately, and it is the most important number in this file. Madagascar's real output per head FELL for most of the two decades before 1990 - the collapse dates from the nationalisations and the 'investissement a outrance' borrowing spree of 1978-80, and the structural adjustment programmes that ran from 1982 onward stabilised the country without ever restoring growth. Real GDP grew about 1.1% a year across the 1980s against population growth near 2.9%. Set at -0.005, above Zaire's and below the roster's zero cluster: an economy that is getting worse at producing, slowly, which is what the 1990s then confirmed - GDP per head in 2000 was lower than in 1990.
Inflation 11.8%: World Bank FP.CPI.TOTL.ZG, series MDG, 1990 = 11.78.

Interest rate 25.8%: World Bank FR.INR.LEND, series MDG, 1990 = 25.80, the commercial bank lending rate. This is the same convention the rest of the roster uses (see kenya.json's note) rather than the Banque Centrale de Madagascar's taux directeur, which was lower; the field is documented as a policy rate and this is a stated substitution of the lending rate for it, consistent across the roster. Real rate +14.0 points, punishing, and the correct picture of a country under adjustment defending a franc malgache that was devalued repeatedly across the decade. The loader's coupled check reads 0.025 - (0.258 - 0.118) = -0.115.

Revenue 7.9% of GDP: World Bank GC.REV.XGRT.GD.ZS, series MDG, 1990 = 7.93, revenue excluding grants. THE LOWEST TAX TAKE IN THE ROSTER and not a data error - it is the fiscal side of the same collapse. A state that collects under a tenth of its output is a state that cannot pay its army, its teachers or its customs officers, and the whole of what happened to Madagascar in 1991 follows from that more than from anything in its politics.
Military 1.2% of GDP: World Bank MS.MIL.XPND.GD.ZS, series MDG, 1990 = 1.23.

Investment 22% state / 14% private, summing to 36% of GDP: FLAGGED AS THE WEAKEST FIGURE IN THIS FILE, and the caveat is stated rather than buried. World Bank NE.GDI.TOTL.ZS, series MDG, 1990 = 35.96 is what the series says and 35.96 is what is entered. It is not credible as a real investment ratio: the same table reads 17.60 in 1988, 40.75 in 1989, 35.96 in 1990, 30.67 in 1991. No economy raises its investment share by 23 points of GDP in one year and Madagascar, of all economies, did not do it in 1989. What the number almost certainly is, is an artefact of valuing an aid-financed import bill of capital goods at border prices against a domestically-deflated GDP while the franc malgache was being devalued - the accounts are internally consistent and the ratio is still not a measure of productive capacity. It is entered as the sourced figure rather than replaced by a guess, per the rule that the series the roster sits on wins; the split is put 22/14 toward the state because the public investment programme financed by the IMF and the World Bank is what the spending actually was. A QA reader who thinks this should have been bracketed down to the high teens has a good argument and this note is where it is conceded. What stops the model reading Madagascar as a high-investment miracle is the negative TFP trend and the 98%-of-GNI debt sitting beside it.

Debt 98% of GDP: World Bank DT.DOD.DECT.GN.ZS, series MDG, 1990 = 98.16, external debt stocks as a share of GNI. Near a full year of national income owed abroad. Madagascar reached HIPC decision point in 2000 on the strength of exactly this.
Oil 0.0: no production. The Bemolanga tar sands and the Tsimiroro heavy oil were known and undeveloped and still are.

System Command: the Second Republic's constitution of 1975 declared a socialist state, the banks, the insurers and the import trade had been nationalised, and SINPA held the rice monopoly. Entered the same way tanzania.json is entered and for the same reason - both were declared socialist economies that were simultaneously under IMF adjustment by 1990, and the enum has two arms. The liberalisation was real and partial: import detaxation from 1988, the rice trade freed, but the parastatals were still there and the state still allocated foreign exchange.

Authoritarianism 0.65 and stability 45: Didier Ratsiraka had governed since 1975 and was re-elected on 12 March 1989 with 62.7% against three opponents, a result the opposition rejected and which was followed by rioting in Antananarivo. Parties existed only inside the Front National pour la Defense de la Revolution until the constitutional revision of March 1990 removed the requirement - two months after the game opens, and nothing here schedules it. Stability 45 is set below Kenya's and above Ethiopia's: a regime with fifteen years in office, no armed challenger, a bankrupt treasury and an urban population that had stopped believing it. The Forces Vives general strike that paralysed the country from May 1991 and the Avenue de l'Independance shootings of 10 August 1991 are not written in anywhere and should not be; they are what a model with these numbers ought to be able to produce.

Separatism 0.06: the cotier/Merina division is the axis of Malagasy politics - Ratsiraka is Betsimisaraka from Toamasina and built his coalition against the highland Merina - and the federalist movement that armed itself in 1991-92 came out of it. It is a quarrel about who runs the state rather than about leaving it; no province had a secessionist movement in January 1990. Set at 0.06, below Zimbabwe's 0.08 and well below the Comoros' 0.25 on the next island over, where the strain really is territorial.

Military strength 1.8: about 21,000 in the armed forces plus a 7,500-strong gendarmerie, largely immobile, with a handful of Soviet-supplied MiG-21s that mostly did not fly. Set above Senegal's 1.5 on numbers and below what those numbers would suggest on any other measure, because an army whose government collects 7.9% of GDP is an army that is not paid. Madagascar has never fought a foreign war and its army's only political act of the period was to refuse to fire, in 1991.

pop_growth_1990 = 2.9232%/yr. Compound annual growth of World Bank SP.POP.TOTL, series MDG (Madagascar): 10,134,550 in 1984 to 11,704,998 in 1989 — the five years ending on the eve of the 1 January 1990 start date. See EconomyRecord::pop_growth_1990 in spheres-sim/src/data/mod.rs for why the window ends in 1989 and not with the single-year 1990 rate.

reserves_bn = 0.245 ($bn). Total reserves including gold, MDG, 1989: US$245265708.20 (World Bank World Development Indicators series FI.RES.TOTL.CD, 'Total reserves (includes gold, current US$)', retrieved from the World Bank API on 2026-09-02; indicator lastupdated 2026-07-13). THE 1989 OBSERVATION AND NOT THE 1990 ONE: a reserve is a stock, and the stock on the morning of the 1 January 1990 start date is the end-1989 figure - the same reasoning pop_growth_1990 above gives for ending its window on 31 December 1989. LIMIT STATED: this series is official reserve assets. Sovereign wealth fund balances are not in it and none has been added, because no audited 1990 balance could be sourced for any of them; where that materially understates a state's usable stock it is reported rather than estimated (iron rule 4).

note: 1990 TECHNOLOGY: AUTHORED, NOT DERIVED. What this nation knew on 1 January 1990 is transcribed and sourced grant by grant, exactly like every other 1990 figure in this file, and is not read off tfp_trend - there was never a code path from the trend to the known set, and the zero that stood there was a claim about the world rather than an absence of one (BIBLE section 8 and iron rule 4, both amended 2026-08-30). THE PREDICATE IS SPLIT, and split by the technology's OWN EFFECT TYPE so that it is mechanically computable and never a per-nation judgement call. A node whose effects include MilitaryEfficiency, MilitaryStrength, DiffusionEmission or CostReduction is SOVEREIGNTY-SIDE: holding it means this nation could PRODUCE it, so operating an imported article does not qualify. Every other node is USE-SIDE: deployed and in operational use here is enough, whoever built it, because the effect such a node pays is a productivity, health or output effect and that effect is real in the country where the machine runs. Of the 48 technologies the tree lets anyone hold in 1990, 17 are sovereignty-side and 31 are use-side.

DATA-KEYED TAIL NATION. This nation is outside the 29 authored majors, so nothing here was authored technology by technology: a grant is made only where one of two named published global series supports it, and nothing is modelled, estimated or interpolated. A short list, or an empty one, is the correct outcome of that rule and not a gap in the work.

Data-keyed tail nation: not one of the 29 authored majors. Only the two series named in ruling 3 were consulted - WHO/UNICEF WUENIC DTP3 1990 and World Bank IT.CEL.SETS. Nothing was modelled, estimated or interpolated, and no other evidence was admitted. ISO3 key used for both series: MDG.
AUTHORED, AND THE ANSWER IS NOTHING. Both named series were checked and both refused this nation; the empty grant list is a finding, not an absence of work.
WUENIC DTP3 1990 = 46% against the 80% UCI-1990 threshold: refused.
IT.CEL.SETS at 31 December 1989 = 0 against a threshold of any positive count: refused.

The other 46 grantable 1990 technologies are BLANK for this nation by design, not by oversight: the 17 sovereignty-side entries are unreachable by any use-in-operation series, and no published global series was named that keys the remaining 29 use-side entries.
